title: Economic Batch Advisor: workload profiling and safe rollout playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build and ship the Economic Batch Advisor: a continuous recommendation engine that synthesizes workload profiles, KV/prefix cache signals, and inference economics to produce safe, explainable batching and caching configurations. The Advisor must emit candidate parameter sets (microbatch size, coalescing windows, KV-tiling hints, cache TTL) with a risk score and rollback plan, integrate with Console for human review, and support automated canary and shadow applies with automatic rollback when SLO or quality regressions are detected. Goal: reduce token cost per request by 12–20% on medium-tail workloads without increasing 99th percentile latency beyond configured SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Advisor produces per-workload candidate configs with risk_score and rationale for >90% of profiled workloads
Automated shadow-apply runs against ~5% of traffic and captures latency/cost/quality deltas in telemetry
Canary rollout framework applies safe-config to a targeted cohort and auto-rolls back on defined guardrails
Console UI shows recommendations, underlying signals, and a one-click apply flow with a required human approval for high-risk ops
End-to-end integration tests covering rollback triggers (latency breach, error spike, output-quality regressions) pass in CI
implementation_steps: Design workload signature: combine arrival patterns, median/99 latency, KV hit rate, prefix share, sequence-length histogram
Train/derive heuristics: cost-vs-latency frontier by microbatch size and coalescing window for representative model classes
Risk scoring: simulate worst-case latency tail using sampled traces and apply safety margins per customer tier
Telemetry pipeline: add metric tags and events (candidate_id, apply_type) and store deltas for automated evaluation
Shadow runner: implement transparent shadow-apply that routes copies of requests to candidate config without impacting production responses
Canary engine: phased apply with configurable phases (1pct -> 5pct -> 20pct) and pre/post comparison windowing
Console & API: expose recommendations, detailed signal view, approval flow and force-rollback button
E2E tests & chaos scenarios: latency injection, KV cache eviction events, and synthetic output-quality regressions
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Lab profiling and simulation against historical traces (internal only)
Stage 1: Shadow runs on selected beta customers (non-intrusive)
Stage 2: Canary auto-apply with human-in-the-loop approval for P1/P0 customers
Stage 3: Gradual expanded automation with policy-driven gating per customer tier
Rollback policy: immediate rollback on latency SLO breach (>5pct over baseline 99p for 5m) or error-rate spike (>3x baseline) or quality regression detected by eval hooks
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: microburst workloads could see tail latency regressions — Mitigation: conservative microbatch ceilings + KV-aware tiling when burstiness detected
Risk: silent quality regressions from quantized/altered execution paths — Mitigation: run lightweight eval prompts during shadow runs and require human approval if quality delta > threshold
Risk: cascading rollback noise across many workloads — Mitigation: staggered rollback windows and per-customer rate-limits on concurrent rollbacks
Risk: telemetry lag hides regressions — Mitigation: prioritize near-real-time delta metrics for canaries and require 2-way health signals before progressing phases
